_fixture: RETURNS_ORDER_SF_ORD009 — Swagger-shaped create body for POST /api/order/customerOrders. The DEDICATED disposable order of storefront case ORD-009 (014-orders-frontend.csv) — submit a return for ALL items with a reason. Completed, fully delivered today in one shipment, two eligible lines ordered 4 and 2.
_why: The case submits a return and has no Cleanup, so it gets its own order: a shared one is drained by the first case that runs. The seeder REBUILDS this order whenever a return on it still holds units (rebuildWhenHeld). A line is returnable only once its shipment carries a DeliveryDate, which the shared COMPLETED_ORDER never has.
_contract: Every `_`-prefixed key is FIXTURE METADATA, stripped by the seeder before the POST. Line identity comes from live discovery; delivery dates come from `_deliveryOffsetDays` resolved against seed-time now. There is NO literal date and NO runtime GUID in this file — the created order id, its line item ids and the resolved delivery instants are written to test-data/aliases.<env>.json.
_seedPhases: PHASE 1 POST creates the order (the platform ASSIGNS line item ids and IGNORES client-supplied ones, so shipment items cannot be linked at create). PHASE 2 PUT stamps shipments[].items[] with the assigned lineItemId + the inline lineItem object (without the inline object the platform silently drops the shipment item) and the shipment deliveryDate. Line order is NOT preserved by the platform, so lines are matched by SKU, never by index.

items._note: Line A (role lineX) — productId/sku/name are placeholders; the seeder live-discovers a real catalog product for the target env and stamps them in.
items.name: AGENT-TEST Returns SF009 Line A

items._note: Line B (role lineY) — a distinct product from line A and a DIFFERENT quantity, so which line went into the return is observable.
items.name: AGENT-TEST Returns SF009 Line B

shipments._note: ONE shipment delivering every line in full today (offset resolved at seed time — never a literal date).
